outcome: height and weight compliance rate at 6 months
cohort: The study included 2063 pregnant women over 28 weeks of gestation, some infected with SARS-CoV-2 and others not, and their subsequent newborns.
finding: While SARS-CoV-2 infection during late pregnancy was associated with higher newborn SARS-CoV-2 infection rates and longer neonatal hospital stays, it did not significantly impact most other neonatal complications or growth and development at six months.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate did not significantly differ between infected and non-infected participants.
